correctness.rationale: Forest orbit quotient acyclicity follows from rooted barycentric subdivision at group-fixed centers, extending by component stabilizers. The barycentric orbit map is a two-sided PL identification of subgroup-fixed spaces. The preexisting forest dominance theorem supplies exact matching-number sphere dimensions; the reduced Lefschetz formula produces the stated integral sign. The 42-forest verifier checks 921 subgroup actions and 1,301 individual traces. Finite tests are corroborative only.

Neither theorem asserts this all-subgroup PL correspondence.

value.rationale: The theorem answers the natural all-subgroup topology and integral orientation questions for an infinite canonical graph-complex class; it reduces arbitrary forest symmetries to matching numbers of explicit quotient forests. Two-edge-arm trees give an exact all-subgroup fixed-sphere profile and the nontrivial full symmetric-group sign character. It is not claiming the known ordinary forest sphere dimension as new.
